title: Assistance for Victims of Incident Involving Address Changes Via ICA System, Punishment for Perpetrators and Remedial Actions to Correct System or Process
what_it_is: Assistance for Victims of Incident Involving Address Changes Via ICA System, Punishment for Perpetrators and Remedial Actions to Correct System or Process

sections.label: Unauthorised address changes and ICA review
sections.summary: Questions asked whether unauthorised address changes affected CDC Vouchers and benefits, and whether ICA will review past proxy address changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the recent cases of unauthorised change of address using ICA's e-service have affected other Government services such as the distribution of CDC Vouchers and the calculation of Government benefits payable to the affected individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority will be conducting a comprehensive review of all electronic change of addresses done within the past six months through the “Others” module, which allows the change of address by a proxy, to ascertain the authenticity of the change of addresses.

sections.label: ICA address change attempts
sections.summary: ICA found suspects tried to change registered addresses of 99 individuals and succeeded for 71 of them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ICA has found that the suspects tried to change the registered addresses of 99 individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: They succeeded in changing the addresses of 71 of the individuals.

sections.label: Charges under Computer Misuse Act
sections.summary: Four men were charged under the Computer Misuse Act 1993, with penalties of up to three years' imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Four men have already been charged in court for offences under the Computer Misuse Act 1993.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: These offences carry penalties of imprisonment of up to three years, a fine of up to $10,000, or both, for first-time offenders.

sections.label: Guidelines and Personal Data Protection Act
sections.summary: Organisations that fail to comply with these Guidelines may breach their obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Organisations that fail to comply with these Guidelines may be in breach of their obligations under the Personal Data Protection Act.

sections.label: ICA suspends eCOA service
sections.summary: After an internal assessment, ICA suspended the eCOA service on 11 January 2025, and says it could have ceased it earlier in December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Following an internal assessment, ICA decided to suspend the eCOA service and did so on 11 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In hindsight, ICA could have taken steps to cease the service earlier in December 2024 when the modus operandi was established.
